skill.name: deploy-to-vercel
skill.description: Deploy applications and websites to Vercel using preview-first CLI, git, or fallback deployment flows.
skill.summary: Guides agents through safe Vercel preview deployments and fallback deployment paths.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: Most markdown backtick and shell-substitution alerts are formatting or quoted helper commands. Real risks remain in the fallback scripts because they upload project archives to fixed external deployment endpoints and poll returned URLs. No prompt injection text was found, but Archive.zip is an unnecessary binary review blind spot.

remediation.issue: Fallback deployment uploads project archives to fixed external endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent before fallback upload and document the exact endpoints and data sent.

remediation.issue: The git path uses broad commit and push commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show the pending diff and run a secret review before committing or pushing deployment changes.

remediation.issue: Returned preview URLs are polled without domain validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that preview URLs use expected Vercel domains before making follow-up network requests.

remediation.issue: Archive.zip is bundled with duplicate executable resources.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the archive from the published skill or publish only fully reviewable source files.

semantic_findings.title: Project Archive Upload to External Deployment Service
semantic_findings.description: The fallback flow packages project files and posts the tarball to fixed deployment endpoints, then returns public preview and claim URLs. This can disclose source or unpublished content if run without clear consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose instructs fallback deployment and both scripts post the generated tarball to external endpoints. The data flow and public deployment outcome are explicit.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Git Commit and Push Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The git deployment path instructs agents to add all files, commit, and push after one approval. Without a diff or secret review, unrelated files or credentials could be published.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented flow explicitly uses broad git add, commit, and push commands. The risk depends on local project contents, but the workflow is clear.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Returned URL Polling
semantic_findings.description: The scripts parse previewUrl from the deployment response and curl it without checking the host. A compromised or unexpected response could drive outbound requests to unintended destinations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The URL is derived from an external response and then used in curl. The script discards the body, so impact is limited but real.

content.value_statement: Publishing a local app can be slow when git, Vercel linking, and team scope are unclear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through preview-first Vercel deployment flows.
actual_capabilities: Checks git remotes, Vercel linkage files, CLI authentication, and available teams.
Chooses preview deployments by default and uses production only on request.
Supports git-push deployment for linked repositories after explicit user approval.
Runs Vercel CLI link and deploy flows for authenticated projects.
Packages projects for no-auth fallback deployment and returns preview and claim URLs.
Detects common JavaScript frameworks from package.json before fallback deployment.
limitations: Fallback scripts upload project archives to external Vercel deployment endpoints.
The skill does not fetch the deployed page to verify final rendering.
CLI login and git push may fail in sandboxed or non-interactive environments.
It does not perform full secret scanning before committing or packaging files.

use_cases.title: Ship a Preview Build
use_cases.description: Deploy a local app to Vercel and receive a preview URL for review.

use_cases.title: Link a Repository
use_cases.description: Connect an existing repository to a Vercel project and prepare future git-push deployments.

use_cases.title: Deploy from a Sandbox
use_cases.description: Use fallback deployment when normal Vercel authentication is unavailable.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Deploy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a safe default deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy this app to Vercel as a preview. Use the safest available method and show me the deployment link.

prompt_templates.title: Check Then Deploy
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants state checks before deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Vercel project state, tell me whether it is linked, and deploy a preview after I approve any git push.

prompt_templates.title: Team Scoped Deploy
prompt_templates.scenario: Project must deploy under a specific Vercel team.
prompt_templates.prompt: Link this repository to the correct Vercel team, prefer preview deployment, and explain which account or team you used.

prompt_templates.title: Audited Deployment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user wants a review before files leave the machine.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the deployment path first, list files that will be committed or uploaded, then deploy only after I approve the final plan.

output_examples.input: Deploy my app to Vercel as a preview.
output: The skill checks git, Vercel linkage, CLI authentication, and team context.
It selects the preview deployment route and returns the preview URL.
If fallback deployment is used, it also returns a claim URL.

output_examples.input: My sandbox cannot log in to Vercel.
output: The skill tries the CLI path first when available.
If authentication is blocked, it can use the no-auth fallback script.
It explains that the fallback uploads a project archive and needs network access.
The skill treats production deployment as explicit only.
It asks before any git push, then reports the resulting deployment link.
For non-production branches, it expects Vercel to create a preview deployment.

best_practices: Ask for explicit approval before git push or fallback archive upload.
Review the file list and remove secrets before deployment.
Use preview deployments until the user clearly requests production.
anti_patterns: Do not run fallback deployment without explaining that project files are uploaded.
Do not commit every local change without showing the user the pending diff.
Do not deploy production when the user only asked for a preview.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy to production by default?
faq.answer: No. It uses preview deployments unless the user explicitly requests production.

faq.question: Does it require Vercel CLI authentication?
faq.answer: The preferred paths use the Vercel CLI. A fallback script is available when authentication is unavailable.

faq.question: What files can the fallback script upload?
faq.answer: It packages the project directory, excluding node_modules, git data, and .env files. Other sensitive files may still be included.

faq.question: Can it choose a Vercel team?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists available team slugs and uses the selected team scope for later Vercel commands.

faq.question: Does it verify the deployed page?
faq.answer: No. The skill reports the deployment URL and does not fetch the final page for visual verification.

faq.question: Is git push automatic?
faq.answer: No. The instructions require explicit user approval before committing and pushing changes.
